snapshot.title: TNPSC Geography: Rivers & Water Resources of TN
snapshot.exam_hook: 🎯 TNPSC Geography Hook: Thamirabarani: Perennial. Cauvery: Hogenakkal entry. Mettur: Cauvery. Vaigai: Madurai. Kallanai: World's oldest dam.

quick_notes.title: River Cauvery (Kaveri)
quick_notes.detail: Origin: Talakaveri (Kodagu, Karnataka). Enters TN at Hogenakkal falls. Major Tributaries : Bhavani, Amaravathi, Noyyal, Arkavathi. It divides into Coleroon and Cauvery at Srirangam. Delta is the "Granary of South India".
quick_notes.explanation: River Cauvery, also spelled Kaveri, begins at a place called Talakaveri in the Kodagu district of Karnataka. It flows into Tamil Nadu at the Hogenakkal waterfalls. The river's main tributaries, which are smaller rivers that flow into it, are the Bhavani, Amaravathi, Noyyal, and Arkavathi. At the town of Srirangam, the Cauvery splits into two branches: one branch is called the Coleroon and the other keeps the name Cauvery. The area where these branches spread out and deposit rich soil before reaching the sea is called a delta, and this Cauvery delta is known as the "Granary of South India" because it grows a huge amount of rice.

quick_notes.title: Palar & Ponnaiyar
quick_notes.detail: Palar: Origin in Karnataka (Kolar), flows through Vellore/Kanchipuram. Ponnaiyar : Origin in Karnataka, flows through Dharmapuri/Cuddalore. Sathanur Dam is on Ponnaiyar.
quick_notes.explanation: Palar and Ponnaiyar are two rivers that flow through the southern Indian states of Karnataka and Tamil Nadu. Both rivers begin in the state of Karnataka, with the Palar originating near the town of Kolar in Karnataka. After leaving Karnataka, the Palar river enters Tamil Nadu and passes through the districts of Vellore and Kanchipuram. The Ponnaiyar river also starts in Karnataka, then flows into Tamil Nadu and travels through the districts of Dharmapuri and Cuddalore. A dam called Sathanur Dam is built on the Ponnaiyar river.

quick_notes.title: Vaigai & Thamirabarani
quick_notes.detail: Vaigai: Origin in Varushanadu hills, flows through Madurai. Thamirabarani : Origin in Pothigai hills. It is the ONLY perennial (year-round) river in TN due to both monsoons. Famous for "Copper" contents.
quick_notes.explanation: The Vaigai River starts in the Varushanadu hills and flows through the city of Madurai. The Thamirabarani River starts in the Pothigai hills. A perennial river is one that flows with water all year long, even during the dry season. The Thamirabarani is the only perennial river in the state of Tamil Nadu (TN) because it receives water from both the southwest monsoon and the northeast monsoon, which are the two rainy seasons in the region. The Thamirabarani is also famous for having copper in its water, which is why its name means "copper leaf" in Tamil.

quick_notes.title: Other Rivers
quick_notes.detail: Vellar, Thenpennai, Chittar, Gundar. Most TN rivers flow from West to East into the Bay of Bengal.
quick_notes.explanation: Tamil Nadu, often shortened to TN, is a state in southern India. The Vellar, Thenpennai, Chittar, and Gundar are four rivers that flow within Tamil Nadu. A river is a large, natural stream of fresh water that moves across land. The Bay of Bengal is the large body of water located east of India. Almost all rivers in Tamil Nadu, including these four, begin in the western part of the state and travel eastward until they empty into the Bay of Bengal. This means the water from these rivers ends up in the ocean on the eastern coast.

quick_notes.title: Major Dams & Projects
quick_notes.detail: Mettur Dam (Cauvery) - Stanley Reservoir. Kallanai (Grand Anicut) - built by Karikala Chola. Lower Anaicut. Bhavani Sagar. Mullaiperiyar (on Periyar river, supplying water to TN).
quick_notes.explanation: A dam is a large wall built across a river to hold water. The Mettur Dam is a dam built across the Cauvery River. The water stored behind this dam is called the Stanley Reservoir. The Kallanai, also known as the Grand Anicut, is a very old dam built by the Chola king Karikala, and it is also on the Cauvery River. The Lower Anaicut is another dam located downstream on the same river. The Bhavani Sagar Dam is built across the Bhavani River, a tributary of the Cauvery. The Mullaiperiyar Dam is built across the Periyar River in Kerala, and it was constructed to supply water to the state of Tamil Nadu (TN).

topic_title: TNPSC Geography: Rivers & Water Resources of TN
lesson_intro: Today we master the 'Lifelines of Tamil Nadu'. Unlike the perennial rivers of the North, TN rivers are rain-fed and seasonal. The Cauvery is the 'Dakshina Ganga' and the most important river for the state's agriculture. We also study the Vaigai, the Thamirabarani (only perennial river in TN!), and the major dams like Mettur and Kallanai. For TNPSC, knowing the origin points and tributaries of these rivers is a frequent exam area. Let's trace the water flow today.
